study.question: Can fixed temporal resolution allocated toward the most recent supplied events preserve more target-relevant information than equal blocks at the same learned capacity and scored slot count, and what quality/cost does matched full-event scoring recover? Observation: incumbent click AUC0.660647 beats target10/history10 (0.659840/0.660052) and target20/history20 (0.658761/0.660062); learned target conditioning did not help, and doubling groups increased p95 from about13.7 to18.2ms. No local evidence yet locates information utility by recency. This study tests that unresolved uncertainty rather than assuming a recency advantage.
study.hypothesis: A coarse older/fine recent partition may preserve target-sensitive event details that equal-block averaging removes, without a learned router or extra scorer slots. If event-order recency is the driver, recent10 should outperform BOTH its reversed-width early10 replacement and equal10. Full100 bounds a concrete higher-resolution operator under the same source gates; it is not a theoretical upper bound. This is a prospective hypothesis, not controlled support.

Click/item embedding interference versus auxiliary tasks remains unresolved; shared context and host global dense norm clipping can couple the heads despite local path gates. Separate task metrics and do not assert complete optimizer isolation.
Observed small validation differences can reflect BF16 reduction order, one-seed variation and adaptive selection across many trials. Same-seed consistency replays are not independent support.
